quiz_name: Quiz 1: Nodes, Scenes, and Magic GDScript! 🏰📝

questions.q: What is the primary building block of every object and feature in the Godot Engine?
questions.exp: A Node is the fundamental building block and Lego piece in Godot used to build everything from characters to backgrounds!

questions.q: What do we call a tree-like organization of nodes representing a complete world or screen level?
questions.exp: A Scene is like a playroom where we combine various nodes together to represent a level or menu screen!

questions.q: In the Parent-Child hierarchy inside Godot, what happens to the Child node's properties?
opts: The child inherits properties (like position) from the parent
They override the parent node entirely
They convert to complex text files
questions.exp: The Child node inherits coordinate scales and movements from its Parent node, walking with it everywhere in the game!

questions.q: What is the primary scripting language in Godot, designed to be simple and similar to Python?
questions.exp: GDScript is a sweet, simple scripting language created specifically for Godot, making it very easy for beginners to learn!

questions.q: Which magic keyword do we use to declare a smart box (variable) to store game values?
questions.exp: The keyword 'var' stands for variable, which prepares a smart memory box to hold scores, health, or speeds!

questions.q: If we want to store our hero's health hearts count (e.g. 3) as a whole number, what is the type of data?
questions.exp: An 'int' (integer) data type is used specifically for storing whole numbers without any fractions, like hearts or counts!

questions.q: Which data type stores only two logical choices: true or false?
questions.exp: A 'bool' (boolean) data type holds only true or false choices, telling us if our hero is flying, alive, or grounded!

questions.q: When is the ready() function automatically called in Godot?
opts: Once at the beginning when the scene loads and node enters the tree
questions.exp: The _ready() function runs once like a morning alarm, waking up nodes to configure their initial states!

questions.q: Which fast function is called continuously on every frame to update movements and character positions?
questions.exp: The _process(delta) function runs constantly at high speeds to keep game loops updating movements smoothly!

questions.q: What is the primary benefit of using a Game Engine like Godot?
opts: To provide ready-made tools for physics, rendering, and sound to easily build games
questions.exp: A game engine provides pre-built libraries for graphics, sounds, and physics, saving developers from writing systems from scratch!
